heading: Iteration 3 — the cost-first skill (v2), same brief
html:
After the two runs below, the house skill was rebuilt for cost: a 1.2K-token quick card instead of ~28K of references, a spec-driven page generator (build-screen.py), a one-call verifier (verify-page.ps1), a tool-call budget, Inter as the default face, and ApexCharts with a token theme. The same brief was run again with only that skill.

Where v2's 194K still goes: the generator gave the shell for free, but the brief's bespoke widgets (heatmap, kanban, tasks, notifications, table engine) were still written by the model as two patch scripts (~35K output tokens), and the 17 calls each re-sent a ~50–70K context. The next lever is a widget library for those parts (generator flags such as heatmap, kanban, tasks), which would put a console like this near 100K.

heading: What you are looking at
html: One brief (brief.md, 12 numbered requirements: shell with ⌘K palette, notifications, branch switcher, dark/RTL/density; toolbar; 6 KPIs with sparklines; 3 charts; heatmap; a full data table with sort/search/chips/column chooser/bulk bar/pagination/4 states; kanban; activity; tasks; patient drawer; toasts; confirm modal; URL presets) was given to two agents of the same model in parallel: one told to follow jbelly-ui, one told to follow ui-ux-pro-max. Both had to render in headless Edge and fix compile errors before finishing. The third column is the vendor demo dashboard of a purchased commercial template, rendered locally from its own package, as a yardstick for weight and polish — it was not built for this brief, so content differs.

heading: Visual verdict (human read of the captures)
html:
• jbelly-ui: recognisably its own product — teal/navy sidebar with a 3px start-rail signature, Manrope display numerals, dotted rules, tinted page. All 12 brief items present, including the four table states, bulk bar, kanban, drawer with tabs, palette and notifications. RTL flips the shell and translates navigation and titles; some table content stays English. The 500px view is clean (KPIs stack 1-up, toolbar wraps). Density compact by default (right for an all-day operator).
  • ui-ux-pro-max: also complete and polished — Fira Sans/Code, teal primary, filled sparklines, a heatmap with printed values, five programme hues with distinct dashes. RTL is fully translated (nav, titles, KPI labels, legends). Visually it sits closer to the generic “teal SaaS dashboard” look; the catalogue's first suggestion was Neumorphism and the agent had to overrule it.
  • Commercial template: the cleanest chrome per pixel (Inter, hairline cards, 3-column grid) but a marketing-style demo: 4 social KPIs, one chart, a promo card, one 6-row table. No loading/empty/error states, no palette, no Esc/⌘K handlers, 139 raster images. Dark and RTL work.

heading: Cost and time — why the skill runs were long
html:
RunTokensMinutesTool callsWhere the tokens went
jbelly-ui, complex398,11155.390Read SKILL.md + 5–6 references (~20–28K tokens) once, then every later call re-sent them; wrote a 150 KB page in 5 parts (~40K output tokens, slow); then a long self-verification loop — captures at 5 sizes × 3 states, a 47-step scripted smoke test, three fix cycles. 90 tool calls with a 60–90K context each is where ~300K of the 398K went. Thorough, but 2.3× the cost of the other run for a page the deterministic grader rates one point higher.
ui-ux-pro-max, complex246,24424.554~10 search-script invocations with long ASCII output, 144 KB page written in parts, many render/verify cycles (54 calls is the cost driver: each re-sends the whole context).
jbelly-ui, simple (iteration 1)157,84020.324Same reference reading; smaller page.
ui-ux-pro-max, simple155,64416.037
no skill, simple72,4945.41One write, no reads, no render; the cheapest by far and it shows (238 raw palette classes, no states, no keyboard).

The mechanism. Agent cost is Σ(context × steps). Reading 28K tokens of references then making 24–54 tool calls multiplies that reading by the number of calls. Output tokens are the slow part: ~150 KB of HTML ≈ 40K output tokens at roughly 50–80 tokens/s is 8–13 minutes of pure generation, plus renders at ~30 s each.

heading: How to cut the cost (implemented in the skill today)
html:
1. Quick card instead of the full references — references/quick-card.md (~1.2K tokens) carries tokens, sizes and the 20 most-used recipes; the full references (~28K) are opened only for what the card lacks. Expected: −20K context, and −20K × every later call.
  2. Zero-token scaffold — scripts/new-screen.ps1 copies the shell (tokens, sidebar, header, toolbar, KPI, table with 3 states, drawer, palette, toasts) with the personality preset applied. The model edits ~40% of a page instead of composing 100%. Expected: −40–50% output tokens and time.
  3. Read once, batch, never re-read; write once; render once — a hard budget of ≤ 12 tool calls per screen (the runs above used 24–90). At the same context size, halving calls halves the quadratic term.
  4. Route implementation to Class B (Sonnet-class) with the skill; keep Class A for the personality decision and the final review. Same token count, roughly 40% lower price.
  5. Prompt caching — the skill files are static: read them first, before any volatile content, so the cached prefix is reused across calls (cache read ≈ 0.1× price).
  6. Split big pages by contract — for a console of this size, have one call produce the page from a small JSON spec (nav, KPIs, columns) through the scaffold, and separate calls only for the two or three bespoke widgets. Boilerplate should never be model output.

Rough expectation for the same brief after these changes: ~90–120K tokens and 8–12 minutes for the house skill, with the same or better grade. Verify with an iteration-3 run before trusting the number. The biggest single lever is the call budget: the house run's 90 calls, not its references, made it the most expensive.

heading: Grader notes
html: The 8 heuristic checks are deterministic string tests, not judgement. Two failures for ui-ux-pro-max are false negatives: the font check requires a Google Fonts family= import and the personality check flags any blue-hue token and tripped on the page's info colour, not its primary; the height check looks for utility heights and the page sets heights in component classes. The “one primary” failure for both skill runs counts bg-primary on the active nav item and the bulk bar; visually each page has a single primary action. Treat the grades as a smoke test; the captures and the metrics table are the evidence.
